evidence.label: Expected amenable subalgebras preserving core commutants
Bounded recovery for modular spectral averages

headline: Claims every expected inclusion of von Neumann algebras holds an amenable piece with the same commutant in the core.
scope: Inclusions N ⊂ M of von Neumann algebras with separable preduals and a faithful normal conditional expectation. It also treats bicentralizers of type III₁ factors.
plain: A commutant is everything that commutes with a given set of operators. This paper asks whether a tame, amenable part of an algebra N can force the same commutation rules as all of N. It claims yes, inside a larger setting called the continuous core, for every expected inclusion with separable preduals. That settles Marrakchi's relative bicentralizer conjecture, if the proof holds. A companion paper proves, with a Lean check, a bounded recovery theorem used for the absolute bicentralizer problem.
doesNot: This does not cover algebras without separable preduals, and Lean does not check the main theorem or the absolute bicentralizer result.
origin: This result comes from an unreleased OpenAI model, published in the openai/math release on 6 October 2026.

scorecard.firstStepBy: Alain Connes, bicentralizer problem in the classification of injective factors
scorecard.significanceWhy: It claims to settle the relative bicentralizer conjecture, a recent open problem in the structure of type III von Neumann algebras.

explanation:
Start with 2-by-2 matrices. Which matrices commute with D = diag(1, 2)? Write a general matrix with entries a, b in the top row and c, d below. Multiplying by D on the right gives a, 2b, c, 2d. Multiplying on the left gives a, b, 2c, 2d. These agree only when b = 0 and c = 0. So the matrices commuting with D form a 2-dimensional set, the diagonal ones. Now also ask them to commute with the swap matrix, which has 1s off the diagonal. That forces a = d. Only multiples of the identity survive. Two well-chosen matrices impose the same rule as all four dimensions of matrices.

The set of everything commuting with a collection is its commutant. In infinite dimensions, the analogous question is harder. Take a von Neumann algebra N inside a larger one, M. Can a tame part P of N impose exactly the same commutation constraints as N? Tame here means amenable, also called injective. Popa's 1981 work gave a model for finding such pieces in one setting[1]. The inclusion must also be expected: there is a well-behaved averaging map from M onto N.

The harder setting involves the continuous core. This is a larger algebra that adds unitaries driving the modular flow, a built-in time evolution of type III algebras. Connes introduced the bicentralizer problem in classifying injective factors[2]. Haagerup solved the amenable type III₁ case[3]. Marrakchi formulated the relative bicentralizer conjecture. He proved it is equivalent, for separable preduals, to the statement this paper claims[4]. The obstacle is that the core holds those extra unitaries, so matching commutants inside M alone is not enough.

This paper claims that for every such inclusion there is an amenable P inside N with an averaging map onto P[5]. Its commutant inside the core matches that of N. This would resolve the conjecture, including inclusions with arbitrary centers and types[6]. Houdayer and Marrakchi have announced that every type III₁ factor with a faithful normal state has trivial bicentralizer[7]. The paper gives another proof of the separable case. The companion proves a bounded spectral recovery theorem for states whose centralizer is only scalars[8]. It uses this for another proof of bicentralizer triviality for separable type III₁ factors[9].

How sure is this? A computer proof checker called Lean has a formal proof of the bounded recovery theorem. It turns positive spectral averages into uniformly bounded algebra elements. The main core-commutant theorem and the absolute bicentralizer result are not part of that Lean statement. No specialist review of the papers has been published.
hypeCheck: Major if the main proof holds. Lean checks only the bounded recovery theorem, not the core-commutant theorem or bicentralizer triviality, and no specialist review is published.

glossary.meaning: An algebra of operators on a Hilbert space, closed under adjoints and under weak limits.
A tameness property of von Neumann algebras that allows averaging arguments.
A well-behaved averaging map from a larger algebra onto a smaller one inside it.
A built-in one-parameter time evolution that every faithful state gives a von Neumann algebra.
A larger algebra built from M and the unitaries that drive its modular flow.
A kind of von Neumann algebra with no trace, whose modular flow is as rich as possible.
The elements commuting asymptotically with every bounded sequence that asymptotically commutes with a given state.
A size limit: the algebra is determined by countably many states.
